deviations: The 'incoherent preferences' exclusion is not defined operationally in the paper text. I defined coherent as a 0/1 preference-for-recognition pattern over the 18 intervals that is weakly increasing (incl. constant) or single-peaked (0..1..0); decreasing, dipped, or multi-reversal patterns are incoherent. This reproduces the paper's incoherent counts exactly (40 Prolific, 11 Berkeley, 2 BU among attention-check passers) and the 1.0/1.8/1.7% non-monotonic shares among the coherent.

Prolific: after attention-check and incoherence exclusions 970 participants remain vs 968 in the paper; I additionally dropped the 2 participants with a missing public-recognition group assignment or missing practice-round record (both scored 0-1 points in the public round). This rule is my guess, not stated in the paper. Prolific anonymous-round mean is 809.7 vs paper 807.9 and Table 6 Prolific estimates are close but not identical, so the Prolific sample likely differs slightly from the authors'.
BU sample taken to be the BU QM222 file (121 completes, matching the paper); QM221 is not used.
Round-order dummies: position (1st/2nd/3rd) of each round taken from the Condition string (e.g. 'RAE'); dummies for 2nd and 3rd with 1st omitted.
Table 7 bootstrapped confidence intervals not computed (only point estimates are claimed).
notes: Data: Raw Data/{prolific,berkeley,bu_qm222}_survey_data.csv. Exclusions: failed attention check (non-missing attention_check) and incoherent preferences (see deviations); final N 968/384/118. Table 5: OLS (fixest) of points on public-recognition and paid-round indicators plus round-position dummies, SE clustered by participant; N 2904/1152/354 match. Table 6 col 4 (Berkeley) reproduced exactly: r0=-3.3246, r1=0.3790, r2=-0.00404 (WTP = +pref_rec_X_1 if preference 1, -pref_anom_X_1 if 0; interval midpoints in hundreds of points; >=1700 interval excluded). Berkeley and BU control means (989.8, 815.9) match the paper exactly, yet Table 5 coefficients differ somewhat (Berkeley PR 134.74 vs 134.41; BU PR 115.79 vs 103.61, FI 132.26 vs 118.33), suggesting the authors' order-dummy coding differs from my position coding. Structural Berkeley action-signaling parameters from Appendix F.1: gamma1 = sqrt(r1^2-4 r0 r2), rho = (sqrt(r1^2-4 r2 r0)-r1)/(2 abar r2) with abar = anonymous mean + PR effect, c = (r1+2 r2(a0+tau))/tau, predicted FI effect = 0.5/c (5 cents/10 points = $0.50 per hundred points). Six exploratory runs (attempts 1-6, no RESULT lines) were used to work out the exclusion rule. After the first scored run I ran check_attempt once (reported all claims within tolerance) and did not change the script, so that run is the final run and is not recorded as a claim attempt. Also read (inside the mount, not scripts): Packet/README.pdf and the data dictionary.xlsx strings. No run hung.
